"description": "Brief description of the bundled skills.",

"./skill-a",

readme_clues: [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

You need git and one of [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex), [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli), [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) 2, [Copilot CLI](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli) or [Pi](https://pi.dev), signed in.
The tour is written by an LLM you already use: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot CLI or Pi. `tour` is read-only. It never changes your files or your repository.
Claude Code / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode / Copilot / Pi, started in that directory

They go to the provider of that tool (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google or GitHub; with OpenCode and Pi, the provider of the model you use), under the terms of your account with them. `tour` itself makes no network requests, has no server, and collects no telemetry.
- using MCP servers, plugins, extensions or web search
claude -p --restricted --strict-mcp-config --tools Read,Grep,Glob
- `--strict-mcp-config` loads no MCP servers
- `--ignore-user-config` and `--ignore-rules` skip your `~/.codex` settings and rules, so your MCP servers and plugins are not loaded
- Temporary settings in the export directory register only those four tools, and turn off MCP discovery, sub-agents, hooks, checkpoints and telemetry.
- `--extensions none` loads no extensions. `--allowed-mcp-server-names` is set to a name no server has, so no MCP server starts.
OpenCode: an agent of its own that can only read and search
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent diff-tour

- `tour` passes its own config in `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, which outranks yours. It denies every tool and then allows only `read`, `glob` and `grep`, and the agent `diff-tour` ends with the same rules. Reading outside the export directory is denied.
- Policies, which can only take permissions away, block every other tool too, and every MCP server, skill and plugin.

- `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` points to an empty directory and project config is turned off, so nothing in `~/.config/opencode` (plugins, MCP servers, agents, `AGENTS.md`) and no `opencode.json` or `AGENTS.md` in the repository is loaded. Only `model` and the provider settings are copied from your config, so your model and sign-ins still work.

# Agent Skills
Agent Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that AI agents can discover and use to perform at specific tasks. Write once, use everywhere.
Codex uses skills to help package capabilities that teams and individuals can use to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way. This repository catalogs skills for use and distribution with Codex.

- [Create custom skills in Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills/create-skill)
- [Agent Skills open standard](https://agentskills.io)
## Installing a skill
Skills in [`.system`](skills/.system/) are automatically installed in the latest version of Codex.
To install [curated](skills/.curated/) or [experimental](skills/.experimental/) skills, you can use the `$skill-installer` inside Codex.
Curated skills can be installed by name (defaults to `skills/.curated`):
$skill-installer gh-address-comments
For experimental skills, specify the skill folder. For example:
$skill-installer install the create-plan skill from the .experimental folder
$skill-installer install https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.experimental/create-plan
After installing a skill, restart Codex to pick up new skills.
